get.description: Ordered by language, so a picker renders the same way twice. A product nobody has translated answers an empty list rather than null.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The kind of thing being translated. Only `product` is accepted, because `translateProducts` is the engine's only hook on the public read path — storing a variant row would look like a translation that does not work rather than one that was never wired up.

put.summary: Write one product's translation into one language
put.description: Replaces the whole field set rather than merging it, like every other whole-object PUT here: the caller sent the translation it wants, and a merge would make removing a field impossible. Emptying every field is the same intention as deleting the row, and answers 204 — an empty object left behind would show up as a language this product claims to be translated into.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The kind of thing being translated. Only `product` is accepted, because `translateProducts` is the engine's only hook on the public read path — storing a variant row would look like a translation that does not work rather than one that was never wired up.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: A BCP 47 tag. A regional tag falls back to its primary subtag on read, so a row stored for `fr` serves a shopper asking for `fr-CA`, and an exact `fr-CA` row beats it.

204.description: Every field was empty, so the translation was removed.

delete.summary: Remove one product's translation into one language
delete.description: 204 whether or not a row went: deleting a translation that is not there leaves the world in the state the caller asked for.

fields.description: The translated fields. Only `title`, `description`, `seo_title` and `seo_description` are accepted — an unknown name is refused rather than dropped, because a silently discarded field is a translation somebody believes they wrote. A field left out keeps the product's stored text rather than blanking it.
